title: A directed family of subfields between K^p and K with intersection K^p detects differentials and p-th powers in finite extensions
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, $K$ a field of characteristic $p$ and $K^p=\{a^p:a\in K\}$. Let $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}$ be a family of subfields of $K$ such that (i) $K^p\subseteq K_\alpha$ for all $\alpha$; (ii) $K^p=\bigcap_{\alpha}K_\alpha$; (iii) for $\alpha,\alpha'\in\mathcal A$ there is $\alpha''\in\mathcal A$ with $K_{\alpha''}\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_{\alpha'}$. Let $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ and $\Omega_{K/K_\alpha}$ be the modules of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K/K_\alpha}$ the $K$-linear map with $\mathrm da\mapsto\mathrm da$ (it exists by the universal property, $\mathrm d:K\to\Omega_{K/K_\alpha}$ being in particular an $\mathbf F_p$-derivation). Then: (1) an element $\omega\in\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ whose image in $\Omega_{K/K_\alpha}$ is zero for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A$ is zero; (2) for every finite field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension] we have $L^p=\bigcap_{\alpha}L^pK_\alpha$, where $L^p=\{b^p:b\in L\}$ and $L^pK_\alpha$ is the subfield of $L$ generated by $L^p$ and $K_\alpha$.

proof.text: (A $p$-basis of $K$ and the basis of $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$.) The map $F:K\to K$, $b\mapsto b^p$, is a ring homomorphism ($(b+c)^p=b^p+c^p$ since $p$ divides $\binom pj$ for $0<j<p$), injective as $K$ is a field, so $K^p=F(K)$ is a subfield of $K$ ($(b^p)^{-1}=(b^{-1})^p$); likewise $L^p$ is a subfield of $L$ for every field $L\supseteq K$. The prime field $\mathbf F_p\subseteq K$ satisfies $c=c^p$ for $c\in\mathbf F_p$, so $\mathbf F_p\subseteq K^p$ and $\mathbf F_pK^p=K^p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists] applied to $K$ there is a family $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ in $K$ whose monomials $x^E=\prod_ix_i^{e_i}$ ($E=(e_i)_{i\in I}$, $0\le e_i<p$, almost all $e_i=0$) form a basis of $K$ over $K^p=\mathbf F_pK^p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis] for the extension $K/\mathbf F_p$, $(\mathrm dx_i)_{i\in I}$ is a basis of the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

proof.text: (Proof of (2): the induction and the reduction to extensions without intermediate fields.) For every finite extension $L/K$ and every $\alpha$, $L^p\subseteq L^pK_\alpha$, so $L^p\subseteq\bigcap_\alpha L^pK_\alpha$ (intersection taken in $L$, the empty intersection being $L$); we prove the reverse inclusion by induction on $d=[L:K]$, for all fields $K$ of characteristic $p$, all families $(K_\alpha)$ satisfying (i)-(iii) and all $L/K$ with $[L:K]=d$ simultaneously. If $d=1$, $L=K$ and $K^pK_\alpha=K_\alpha$ by (i), so $\bigcap_\alpha K^pK_\alpha=K^p$ by (ii). Let $d>1$. Suppose first that there is an intermediate field $K\subsetneq M\subsetneq L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] $[L:K]=[L:M][M:K]$ with both factors $>1$, so $[M:K]<d$ and $[L:M]<d$. Put $M_\alpha=M^pK_\alpha\subseteq M$. By induction for $M/K$, $M^p=\bigcap_\alpha M_\alpha$. The family $(M_\alpha)$ of subfields of the field $M$ (of characteristic $p$) satisfies (i)-(iii): $M^p\subseteq M_\alpha$; $M^p=\bigcap_\alpha M_\alpha$; and if $K_{\alpha''}\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_{\alpha'}$ then $M_{\alpha''}\subseteq M_\alpha\cap M_{\alpha'}$. By induction for $L/M$ and $(M_\alpha)$, $L^p=\bigcap_\alpha L^pM_\alpha$, and $L^pM_\alpha=L^pK_\alpha$ since $M^p\subseteq L^p$. Suppose now that $K$ and $L$ are the only intermediate fields. Choose $\theta\in L\setminus K$; then $K(\theta)$ (the smallest subfield of $L$ containing $K$ and $\theta$) is an intermediate field $\ne K$, so $L=K(\theta)$; every element of $L$ is algebraic over $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] (the $d+1$ elements $1,\theta,\ldots,\theta^d$ of the $d$-dimensional $K$-space $L$ are linearly dependent). Either $\theta^p\notin K$ (Step 4) or $\theta^p\in K$ (Step 5); in both cases $\bigcap_\alpha L^pK_\alpha\subseteq L^p$, which completes the induction.

By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] for $	heta$ and for $\varphi$, both $1,	heta,\ldots,	heta^{d-1}$ and $1,\varphi,\ldots,\varphi^{d-1}$ are $K$-bases of $L$, $d=[L:K]$. The Frobenius $F:L	o L^p$, $b\mapsto b^p$, is a ring isomorphism mapping $K$ onto $K^p$ and $F(\sum_jc_j	heta^j)=\sum_jc_j^p\varphi^j$, so $L^p=\{\sum_{j<d}a_j\varphi^j:a_j\in K^p\}$. Fix $\alpha$ and put $W_\alpha=\{\sum_{j<d}a_j\varphi^j:a_j\in K_\alpha\}$. It is a $K_\alpha$-subspace of $L$ containing $K_\alpha$ and, by (i), $L^p$; it is closed under multiplication by $\varphi$ because $\varphi\cdot\varphi^{d-1}=\varphi^d\in L^p\subseteq W_\alpha$, hence it is a subring. It is a field: for $0
e x\in W_\alpha$, $y\mapsto xy$ is an injective $K_\alpha$-linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional $K_\alpha$-space $W_\alpha$ ($L$ is a field), hence surjective, so $x^{-1}\in W_\alpha$. Every subfield of $L$ containing $L^p$ and $K_\alpha$ contains $W_\alpha$; so $L^pK_\alpha=W_\alpha$. Let $x\in igcap_\alpha L^pK_\alpha$ and write $x=\sum_{j<d}c_j\varphi^j$ with $c_j\in K$, uniquely. For each $\alpha$, $x\in W_\alpha$ gives $x=\sum_jc'_j\varphi^j$ with $c'_j\in K_\alpha\subseteq K$, and uniqueness gives $c_j=c'_j\in K_\alpha$. So $c_j\in igcap_\alpha K_\alpha=K^p$ by (ii), and $x\in L^p$.

proof.text: (Case $\theta^p\in K$.) Put $t=\theta^p\in K$. Then $t\notin K^p$: if $t=s^p$ with $s\in K$ then $(\theta-s)^p=\theta^p-s^p=0$, so $\theta=s\in K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] every element of $L=K(\theta)$ is $\sum_{j<d}c_j\theta^j$ with $c_j\in K$, so $L^p=F(L)=\{\sum_{j<d}c_j^pt^j\}$ is contained in the subring $K^p[t]$ of $K$ generated by $K^p$ and $t$; conversely $K^p\subseteq L^p$ and $t=\theta^p\in L^p$. As $t^p\in K^p$, $L^p=K^p[t]=\{\sum_{j<p}a_jt^j:a_j\in K^p\}$. For each $\alpha$ let $U_\alpha=\{\sum_{j<p}a_jt^j:a_j\in K_\alpha\}\subseteq K$; it contains $K_\alpha$ and (by (i)) $L^p$, is closed under multiplication by $t$ since $t^p\in K^p\subseteq K_\alpha$, hence is a subring, finite-dimensional over $K_\alpha$, hence a subfield (as in Step 4), contained in every subfield containing $K_\alpha$ and $L^p$: $L^pK_\alpha=U_\alpha$. (The source writes $U_\alpha$ as a direct sum $\bigoplus_{j<p}K_\alpha t^j$; this fails when $t\in K_\alpha$, and the directedness (iii) is used instead.) By (ii) there is $\alpha_0$ with $t\notin K_{\alpha_0}$. Claim: $1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1}$ are linearly independent over $K_{\alpha_0}$. Indeed $t$ is a root of $X^p-t^p\in K_{\alpha_0}[X]$; let $e=[K_{\alpha_0}(t):K_{\alpha_0}]$; by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] $1,t,\ldots,t^{e-1}$ is a $K_{\alpha_0}$-basis of $K_{\alpha_0}(t)$, so expressing $t^e$ in it gives a monic $m\in K_{\alpha_0}[X]$ of degree $e\ge1$ with $m(t)=0$, and every $g\in K_{\alpha_0}[X]$ with $g(t)=0$ is divisible by $m$ (write $g=qm+r$ with $\deg r<e$; $r(t)=0$ forces $r=0$). So $m$ divides $X^p-t^p=(X-t)^p$ in $K[X]$; since $K[X]$ is a unique factorization domain and $m$ is monic, $m=(X-t)^e$, whose coefficient of $X^{e-1}$ is $-e\,t\in K_{\alpha_0}$. If $e<p$, $e$ is invertible in $\mathbf F_p\subseteq K_{\alpha_0}$ and $t\in K_{\alpha_0}$, a contradiction; so $e=p$, proving the claim. Now let $x\in\bigcap_\alpha U_\alpha$ and write $x=\sum_{j<p}c_jt^j$ with $c_j\in K_{\alpha_0}$ ($x\in U_{\alpha_0}$), uniquely by the claim. Given $\alpha'$, choose by (iii) $\alpha''$ with $K_{\alpha''}\subseteq K_{\alpha'}\cap K_{\alpha_0}$; $x\in U_{\alpha''}$ gives $x=\sum_jc''_jt^j$ with $c''_j\in K_{\alpha''}\subseteq K_{\alpha_0}$, so $c_j=c''_j\in K_{\alpha'}$. Hence $c_j\in\bigcap_{\alpha'}K_{\alpha'}=K^p$ by (ii), and $x\in K^p[t]=L^p$.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks More on Algebra 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields, line 11458) and its proof, with 07P2 and 07P3; statement kept. Proof in 5 steps: a p-basis of K over F_p and the basis dx_i of Omega_{K/F_p} (existing nodes for 07P2 existence and (a)=>(b)); (1) by contradiction, the relations among the x^E forming a subspace V that meets every K_alpha^N by 07P2 (1)=>(2) for K/K_alpha (new node) and hence (K^p)^N by 07P3 (new node, with the nonempty index set made explicit and derived here from omega != 0); (2) by induction on [L:K] with the tower reduction of the source (tower law leaf), then the two cases theta^p not in K and theta^p in K (split this way instead of separable/inseparable, which avoids separability), each with L^pK_alpha identified and the intersection computed via a new Mathlib leaf for the power basis of a simple algebraic extension (Fields 09GN; IntermediateField.adjoin.powerBasis). Source error: in the case theta^p = t in K the source writes L^pK_alpha = sum_j K_alpha t^j as a direct sum, which fails when t is in K_alpha (K = F_p(s,u), K_1 = K^p(s), t = s: L^pK_1 = K_1 has degree p over K^p, not p^2); the conclusion holds by an argument using (iii), written out. 3 new nodes (2 unsplit, 1 Mathlib leaf).

lean.statement: theorem intersection_subfields_differentials (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type u) [Field K] [CharP K p] {ι : Type v} (Kα : ι → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) (h₁ : ∀ α : ι, Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) ⊆ (Kα α : Set K)) (h₂ : Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) = ((⨅ α, Kα α : IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) : Set K)) (h₃ : ∀ α β : ι, ∃ γ : ι, Kα γ ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα β) : (∀ ω : Ω[K⁄ZMod p], (∀ α : ι, KaehlerDifferential.map (ZMod p) (Kα α) K K ω = 0) → ω = 0) ∧ (∀ (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L], Set.range (fun x : L => x ^ p) = ⋂ α : ι, ((Subfield.closure (Set.range (fun x : L => x ^ p) ∪ (algebraMap K L '' (Kα α : Set K))) : Set L)))
